summary: The PIR motion sensor video is the clear winner, with about 1,900 combined views and most of the shares and saves, mainly from Instagram. Every other video got very little: around 20 to 150 views each. The channel is new and the numbers are small, so these are early signals rather than proof. Still, 'everyday device that seems to act by magic' topics and curiosity-gap titles are doing better than anything else.
winningPattern: A familiar sensor or gadget people see in daily life (motion detector, phone, touchscreen, automatic door), a Hindi hook that states a surprising claim ('Motion Sensor Aapko Dekhta Nahi!'), a title built as a myth-bust or a question, and Instagram Reels as the main source of views. The PIR video is the only one that broke out, so the exact reason is still unclear. The strongest guess is the bold 'it doesn't see you' claim combined with a very common device. The Hindi videos with a surprising claim or 'how does my phone know' angle got more shares and saves than plain explainers.
doMore: Open with a bold, slightly shocking claim about a device people use daily, as the PIR title did
Post Hindi Reels on Instagram first, since it brings about 3 to 10 times the views YouTube does
Pick sensors people meet in real life (lights, ATMs, doors, AC, fan remotes) rather than lab parts
Put a clear 'save this' or 'share with a friend' line at the end to raise shares and saves
Repeat the PIR format with sibling topics (motion, heat, light) and compare results before changing anything else
stopDoing: Posting English-only videos with no Instagram version, like the Arduino Uno one, since they reach a much smaller audience
Using plain or technical-sounding titles and hooks (e.g. 'Ultrasonic Sensor Awaaz Se Kaise Dekhta Hai?') without a shocking claim or a relatable scene
nextTopics: Automatic street light turning on at dusk (LDR)

Hand dryer or tap that starts without touching (IR sensor)
